svg.title: Circular-economy effects on European final-energy demand

cc:Work.dc:title: Circular-economy effects on European final-energy demand
cc:Work.dc:description: Changes in European final-energy demand in 2050, with NDC above NDC+LTT and cement, iron and steel, and aluminium columns. Paired bars place OMNIA-ENGAGE on the left and hatched GCAM on the right. Every fuel segment is 100 × (CE carrier energy − no-CE carrier energy) / no-CE total sector energy, using the same model, pathway, sector and year. These segments are percentage-point contributions to the total-energy percentage change; they are not carrier-specific percentage changes. Positive and negative contributions stack independently from zero. Black diamonds and signed labels show the net total-energy percentage change. All six panels share one percentage scale, retaining increases as well as decreases. Exact carrier parents are selected once. GCAM's total-energy reference retains its reported sector parent; Unallocated is the reported parent minus supplied carrier parents in each scenario. Its change remains an unidentified contribution, with no fuel or process attribution. GCAM aluminium's alumina-refining coverage is unconfirmed. Normalisation focuses on within-model CE responses and does not establish agreement in absolute production or energy levels, or harmonise the models' process boundaries. Historical bars are omitted because these are matched-year CE contrasts. OMNIA sums EUE, EUM and EUW; GCAM selects its EU-27 aggregate once. The OMNIA regions include some small non-EU countries and territories. Only medium/high CE applied in the EU enters; EU+ cases are excluded. Raw source quantities, reference totals, exact variables, regions and calculation coefficients accompany every result. A missing, nonfinite or nonpositive reference makes the response undefined.
